content:
If you're using the school's network, they can block any ports or protocols they want. If this is a school account that's managed by them, it would be very easy to just shut off IMAP access in Gmail's settings. Without knowing the gory details, I'm sure they can make it difficult or impossible to manage school-owned Gmail accounts with IMAP clients like Thunderbird.

If you have your own personal Gmail account, and other provider's accounts (Yahoo, Outlook, AOL, etc.) I don't think they can affect those.

So, if my assumptions are correct, my guess is that you won't be able to access your school account with Thunderbird, but you will still be able to access any private, personal email accounts you may have.

It's not right for them to call IMAP "outdated". It's fairly modern, secure, stable, and reliable. I can't imagine why they would want to ban it, unless they're trying to make it easier to monitor the contents of your email.

content:
If you have an intact copy of a profile, you can import its address books with the Import Tool.

- See menu item <tools | import from another thunderbird installation, then next < p></tools>

- Select Choose a profile folder, then Continue

- A browse window will open. Navigate to the saved Profile folder and choose Select Folder (in Windows)

- Deselect everything except for Address Books. Click Continue, then Start Import

If your account is IMAP, you don't need to import your remote messages - they will automatically download.

If you're looking for Local Folders and POP3 folders, I recommend using the add-on "ImportExportTools NG" (https://addons.thunderbird.net/en-US/thunderbird/addon/importexporttools-ng/) to import messages and folders from the saved profile into local folders in your new profile.

By the way, I think you should turn off the auto-update feature to prevent unexpected updates. See <Settings | General | Updates | Check for updates, but let me choose whether to install them>.
